headlines.summary: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms
headlines.article_text: Tesla, SpaceX stocks fall after 2026 midterms Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap in the two days after midterms. As Democrats control the House and Senate, and Texas flips blue, investors expect Musk and his companies to face probes and steeper regulatory hurdles to their AI and merger ambitions. Musk was the biggest backer of GOP candidates and causes in the mid-terms and most of those he backed were defeated by Dem opponents. In this article TSLA SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT SpaceX CEO Elon Musk looks on as President Donald Trump speaks to the press after a meeting with technology executives about artificial intelligence at the White House in Washington, Sept. 29, 2026. Kent Nishimura | AFP | Getty Images Tesla and SpaceX shares declined by about 9% and 11% respectively on Thursday afternoon with investors concerned that Elon Musk, who is CEO of both companies, could face new Congressional probes, and his companies could face stricter regulation following U.S. mid-term elections. The declines, which correlated with a broader tech selloff , brought aggregate market cap losses for SpaceX and Tesla to over $420 billion since Tuesday's close. Musk's wealth, which had topped $1 trillion after SpaceX's IPO in June, is now down below $800 billion, having dropped about $90 billion in the past week, according to Forbes . He is still the richest man in the world. Musk was the biggest donor to GOP candidates and causes in the mid-terms, with his financial contributions exceeding $470 million , the FT first reported. Despite his bolstering the GOP war chest, most of the candidates Musk backed lost their races . Dems won control of both the House and Senate. And in Texas, where both Tesla and SpaceX are headquartered, Democrats James Talarico (Sen. elect) and Gina Hinojosa (Gov. elect) beat long-time Musk allies, Ken Paxton and Greg Abbott. Deutsche Bank analysts wrote in a note out on Wednesday, "While policy is naturally hard to predict, we could envision SpaceX facing some incremental headwinds in this type of backdrop." Texas' Gov. elect Hinojosa "made data centers a major campaign issue," the analysts noted, calling for "a moratorium on new approvals until the legislature passes stronger protections on water use, electricity costs, local control, and incentives," and criticizing tax breaks for large facilities. Tesla and SpaceX are both building out AI infrastructure in Texas, and are planning to build Terafab, a massive facility, which will include a data center and sprawling semiconductor factory, in Grimes County, Texas. SpaceX also plans to build out a "supercomputer" at its Starbase, Texas launch facility and company town, according to company job listings . Deutsche Bank analysts also wrote that SpaceX's Texas compute capacity could now be at risk of delays. Capital expenditures by the company may need to increase to meet the requirements of tighter, anticipated regulations around data center build out, the analysts wrote. Musk and SpaceX have been instructed to preserve records concerning restrictions they imposed on a military version of their Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, CNN first reported , citing an aide to a Democratic Senator. The restrictions hampered the country's ability to defend against attacks by Russia. Additionally, regulatory scrutiny could block chances for Musk to merge SpaceX and Tesla, an idea he has promoted, while acknowledging shareholders' approval would be required first. headlines.title: AI meltdown: Nvidia and Qualcomm drop more than 9%, pushing Nasdaq to worst day since April 2025
headlines.summary: Companies tied to the AI buildout are all selling off as concerns mount about a slowdown following the midterm elections.
headlines.article_text: Qualcomm sinks after earnings, leading postelection chip sell-off Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Companies tied to the AI buildout are all selling off as concerns mount about a slowdown following the midterm elections. The Nasdaq plunged 5.5% on Thursday, its worst day since April 2025. Chipmakers like AMD, Micron and Applied Materials all suffered double-digit percentage drops. In this article QCOM AMD NVDA INTC ARM MU Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 3:12 03:12 Qualcomm's data center business barely offsetting losses in smartphones: Seaport's Jay Goldberg Closing Bell: Overtime Chipmakers plummeted on Thursday, with Nvidia pushing the Nasdaq to its worst day in 19 months, after this week's midterm election results raised concerns on Wall Street that the artificial intelligence buildout is poised to slow down. Neoclouds like CoreWeave tumbled for a second straight day. Qualcomm contributed to the selloff after issuing a disappointing earnings forecast for the current quarter. Qualcomm and Nvidia both dropped more than 9%, with the latter losing almost $450 billion in market cap. The Nasdaq slied 5.5%, its steepest slide since April 2025. The environment has gone from bad to worse for companies intimately tied to AI infrastructure, as the combination of rising interest rates, ballooning capital needs and the Democratic sweep in Congress has led to increased fears that wide swaths of the market are going to be weighed down by too much debt and too little revenue. Read more CNBC tech news OpenAI pledges to halt NDAs in new data center policy proposal after election rebuke Voters rejected AI data centers over resource concerns. Here's why measuring water usage is hard Nintendo Switch 2 sales plunge 41% as price hikes and memory crunch bite Hyperscalers and Apple surge after election results remove investor uncertainty "The technology is still going to continue on in terms of its development, but if there is a slowdown in the actual development and the buildings and the infrastructure and so forth, that's what stocks are going to trade off," said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners, in an interview with CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Advanced Micro Devices , Micron and Applied Materials all suffered double-digit percentage losses on Thursday. Elon Musk , who contributed hundreds of millions of dollars to try and get Republicans elected in Texas and elsewhere, saw shares of his public companies, SpaceX and Tesla , each drop more than 9%. In Tuesday's election, the states with the most ambitious AI data center plans all turned blue. Democrats won key contests for governor and the Senate in Texas and Ohio, while also coming up victorious in the gubernatorial race in Georgia, where Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff also cruised to reelection. There were 41 local ballot measures in 10 states up for a vote on Tuesday that would place restrictions on the construction of data centers in different ways, according to Ballotpedia . Voters sided against data centers in each measure except one in Harwood, North Dakota, according to an analysis by Ballotpedia and additional results gathered by CNBC on Wednesday. On Wednesday night, at the Wall Street Journal Tech conference, Meta President Dina Powell McCormick told the audience that building data centers is "going to be harder" following the elections. She added that one of the victorious governors had said that, "As soon as we get past the inauguration, let's meet because we don't want to lose this investment in our town. We don't want these jobs to go elsewhere," according to the Journal. Meta, like its hyperscaler peers — Alphabet , Amazon and Microsoft — has laid out an ambitious path for infrastructure development, with spending plans that extend well past $100 billion a year. Meta went free cash flow negative in the latest quarter, joining Alphabet and Amazon, which turned negative in the prior period. The hyperscalers each dropped between 2% and 4% on Thursday. Qualcomm stock chart. Qualcomm on Wednesday became the latest chipmaker to report booming growth in its data center business, though it's still a relatively small unit for the company. Qualcomm had $650 million in data center revenue during the quarter, mostly from customizing and connectivity work, CEO Cristiano Amon said. "We don't have a demand issue; it's a supply issue," Amon told CNBC in an interview. "If I had more supply, I would probably be doing better." The problem for Qualcomm and fellow chipmakers Intel and AMD is that the global memory shortage is jacking up prices, making it harder to get key supplies and leading to surging prices for consumer devices. Intel last week reported a 78% jump in data center revenue, but the stock got crushed due to a weaker-than-expected forecast from the memory shortage. And AMD said this week that sales in its data center business more than doubled in the latest period. Investors are looking past the numbers and questioning the sustainability of that growth, and whether buyers of the technology will be able to put it all to use. "There's going to be a knee-jerk reaction, and that could lead to some delays, and that's going to be some concerns, " Richard Clode, a portfolio manager at Janus Henderson, told "Squawk on the Street." "We're not going to solve for that in terms of knowing the answers to that anytime soon, unfortunately." — CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos contributed to this report.
